requirements.title: Core Message and Content Block Types
requirements.rationale: Restricting message and content structures to active text and tool types removes legacy session baggage and eliminates untyped ordered object wrappers.

criteria.action: define Message as a sealed interface implemented exclusively by UserMessage, AssistantMessage, and ToolResultMessage structs
criteria.contract: core.Message is implemented exclusively by UserMessage, AssistantMessage, and ToolResultMessage, sealed against external implementation; core.ContentBlock is implemented exclusively by TextBlock, ThinkingBlock, and ToolUseBlock; ImageBlock, RawBlock, and ToolResultBlock are not declared in core

setup: core package AST and type declarations
check.pseudocode: assert implementsSealedMessage(UserMessage{}); assert implementsSealedMessage(AssistantMessage{}); assert implementsSealedMessage(ToolResultMessage{}); assert implementsContentBlock(TextBlock{}); assert implementsContentBlock(ThinkingBlock{}); assert implementsContentBlock(ToolUseBlock{}); assert !existsType("ImageBlock"); assert !existsType("RawBlock"); assert !existsType("ToolResultBlock")

criteria.action: define ContentBlock as an interface implemented exclusively by TextBlock, ThinkingBlock, and ToolUseBlock structs, omitting ImageBlock, RawBlock, and ToolResultBlock
omit Unknown fields of type jsonx.OrderedObject and Deferred fields of type *DeferredHandle
criteria.contract: UserMessage, AssistantMessage, and ToolResultMessage contain no Unknown jsonx.OrderedObject or Deferred fields; ToolUseBlock contains ID, Name, Input of type json.RawMessage, ThoughtSignature, and omits InputOrder; AssistantMessage declares Effort of type Effort and omits ThinkingLevel, API, and Provider fields

setup: UserMessage, AssistantMessage, ToolResultMessage, and ToolUseBlock type declarations
check.pseudocode: assert !hasField(UserMessage{}, "Unknown"); assert !hasField(UserMessage{}, "Deferred"); assert !hasField(AssistantMessage{}, "Unknown"); assert !hasField(AssistantMessage{}, "Deferred"); assert !hasField(AssistantMessage{}, "ThinkingLevel"); assert !hasField(AssistantMessage{}, "API"); assert !hasField(AssistantMessage{}, "Provider"); assert hasField(AssistantMessage{}, "Effort"); assert !hasField(ToolResultMessage{}, "Unknown"); assert !hasField(ToolResultMessage{}, "Deferred"); assert hasField(ToolUseBlock{}, "ID"); assert hasField(ToolUseBlock{}, "Name"); assert hasField(ToolUseBlock{}, "Input"); assert hasField(ToolUseBlock{}, "ThoughtSignature"); assert !hasField(ToolUseBlock{}, "InputOrder")

criteria.action: retain ID, Name, Input of type json.RawMessage, and ThoughtSignature, while omitting InputOrder
declare Effort for thinking configuration while omitting ThinkingLevel, API, and Provider fields

requirements.title: Core Argument Preparation and Stability
requirements.rationale: Retaining raw message bytes while removing jsonx dependencies guarantees stable argument serialization across tool executions.

criteria.action: define PreparedArguments with fields Raw of type json.RawMessage, Args of type map[string]any, and Coercions of type []schema.Coercion, containing no references to jsonx
criteria.contract: PreparedArguments.Raw is of type json.RawMessage; PreparedArguments.Args is of type map[string]any; PreparedArguments.Coercions is of type []schema.Coercion; PreparedArguments declares no fields of type jsonx.OrderedObject

setup: a PreparedArguments struct instance initialized with raw JSON bytes, parsed map, and coercions
check.pseudocode: p := core.PreparedArguments{Raw: json.RawMessage(`{"k":"v"}`), Args: map[string]any{"k": "v"}, Coercions: nil}; assert typeof(p.Raw) == json.RawMessage; assert typeof(p.Args) == map[string]any; assert typeof(p.Coercions) == []schema.Coercion; assert !hasField(p, "Order")

criteria.condition: PrepareArguments executes for a tool use block without argument mutations or repairs
criteria.action: preserve the original ToolUseBlock.Input bytes in PreparedArguments.Raw verbatim
criteria.contract: PreparedArguments.Raw is identical byte-for-byte to the original ToolUseBlock.Input bytes; PreparedArguments.Args contains the unmarshaled argument values

setup: a tool with a defined InputSchema and a ToolUseBlock with input JSON bytes
check.pseudocode: inputBytes := json.RawMessage(`{"query":"test","limit":10}`); block := core.ToolUseBlock{ID: "t1", Name: "search", Input: inputBytes}; prep, err := core.PrepareArguments(tool, block); assert err == nil; assert bytes.Equal(prep.Raw, inputBytes); assert prep.Args["query"] == "test"

criteria.condition: PrepareArguments executes for a tool with a non-nil PrepareArguments function that mutates arguments
criteria.action: re-encode the updated arguments and update PreparedArguments.Raw with the mutated JSON bytes
criteria.contract: PreparedArguments.Raw is updated with the re-encoded JSON bytes reflecting the mutation; PreparedArguments.Args reflects the mutated argument map

setup: a tool with a non-nil PrepareArguments hook that adds default parameter values
check.pseudocode: tool.PrepareArguments = func(args map[string]any) (map[string]any, error) { args["injected"] = true; return args, nil }; block := core.ToolUseBlock{ID: "t1", Name: "custom", Input: json.RawMessage(`{"v":1}`)}; prep, err := core.PrepareArguments(tool, block); assert err == nil; assert strings.Contains(string(prep.Raw), `"injected":true`); assert prep.Args["injected"] == true

criteria.condition: PrepareArguments encounters arguments failing validation against the tool InputSchema
criteria.action: reject the call and return an error containing the schema validation failure details
criteria.contract: returns zero-value PreparedArguments and non-nil error wrapping the schema validation issue

setup: a tool with an InputSchema requiring an integer property "count"
check.pseudocode: tool := core.Tool{InputSchema: schema.Object(schema.Prop("count", schema.Int()))}; block := core.ToolUseBlock{ID: "t1", Name: "t", Input: json.RawMessage(`{"count":"invalid_string"}`)}; prep, err := core.PrepareArguments(tool, block); assert err != nil; assert len(prep.Raw) == 0; assert prep.Args == nil

requirements.title: Core Provider Interface and Request Structure
requirements.rationale: A single streaming method signature decouples model invocation from provider registries and middleware abstractions.

criteria.action: define ProviderClient as an interface with the single method Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan StreamEvent, error)
criteria.contract: ProviderClient interface contains exactly one method: Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan StreamEvent, error); StreamEvent declares Event of type Event and Err of type error; Request declares System []ContentBlock, Messages Messages, Tools []ToolWire, ToolChoice ToolChoice, MaxTokens *int, Temperature *float64, TopP *float64, StopSequences []string, and Effort Effort

setup: core package provider definitions in core/provider.go
check.pseudocode: var client core.ProviderClient; ch, err := client.Stream(context.Background(), core.Request{}); assert typeof(ch) == <-chan core.StreamEvent; ev := core.StreamEvent{}; assert hasField(ev, "Event"); assert hasField(ev, "Err"); req := core.Request{}; assert hasField(req, "System"); assert hasField(req, "Messages"); assert hasField(req, "Tools"); assert hasField(req, "ToolChoice"); assert hasField(req, "MaxTokens"); assert hasField(req, "Temperature"); assert hasField(req, "TopP"); assert hasField(req, "StopSequences"); assert hasField(req, "Effort")

criteria.action: define StreamEvent as a struct containing Event of type Event and Err of type error

define Request with System of type []ContentBlock, Messages of type Messages, Tools of type []ToolWire, ToolChoice of type ToolChoice, MaxTokens of type *int, Temperature of type *float64, TopP of type *float64, StopSequences of type []string, and Effort of type Effort
omit legacy provider types ProviderRegistry, ProviderStreamOptions, ClientFunc, StreamFunc, APIProvider, Complete, and Dispatch
criteria.contract: ProviderRegistry, ProviderStreamOptions, ClientFunc, StreamFunc, APIProvider, Complete, and Dispatch are not declared in core

setup: core package symbol definitions in core/provider.go
check.pseudocode: assert !existsSymbol("core.ProviderRegistry"); assert !existsSymbol("core.ProviderStreamOptions"); assert !existsSymbol("core.ClientFunc"); assert !existsSymbol("core.StreamFunc"); assert !existsSymbol("core.APIProvider"); assert !existsSymbol("core.Complete"); assert !existsSymbol("core.Dispatch")

criteria.condition: Stream is called with a canceled context or invalid request parameters
criteria.action: return a non-nil error or emit a StreamEvent carrying the terminal error on the channel
criteria.contract: returns a non-nil error immediately or emits a StreamEvent with non-nil Err on the returned channel

setup: a ProviderClient implementation and a canceled context
check.pseudocode: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); cancel(); ch, err := client.Stream(ctx, core.Request{}); if err == nil { ev := <-ch; assert ev.Err != nil } else { assert err != nil }

requirements.title: Order-Preserving Schema Parsing
requirements.rationale: Parsing JSON Schema definitions with jsontext preserves model-visible property declaration order without external ordered map packages.

criteria.condition: schema.Parse is invoked with a valid JSON Schema byte slice containing object properties
criteria.action: decode the schema using encoding/json/jsontext and populate PropertyOrder with property keys in the exact order they appear in the source bytes
criteria.contract: schema.Parse returns a non-nil *Schema with PropertyOrder exactly equal to ['zebra', 'apple', 'mango']

setup: a JSON Schema string with properties authored in non-alphabetical order 'zebra', 'apple', 'mango'
check.pseudocode: raw := []byte(`{"type":"object","properties":{"zebra":{"type":"string"},"apple":{"type":"string"},"mango":{"type":"string"}}}`); s, err := schema.Parse(raw); assert err == nil; assert s.PropertyOrder == []string{"zebra", "apple", "mango"}

criteria.condition: schema.Parse is invoked with a valid JSON Schema byte slice
criteria.action: populate Schema fields Properties, Required, Type, Description, Title, Items, Enum, Const, Nullable, AnyOf, OneOf, and AllOf from corresponding JSON keywords
criteria.contract: Properties map contains child schemas for each property; Required, Type, Description, Title, Items, Enum, Const, Nullable, AnyOf, OneOf, and AllOf match declared JSON keywords

setup: a JSON Schema string declaring full standard schema keywords
check.pseudocode: raw := []byte(`{"type":"string","description":"test","title":"Test","enum":["a","b"],"const":"a","nullable":true}`); s, err := schema.Parse(raw); assert err == nil; assert s.Type == schema.TypeString; assert s.Description == "test"; assert s.Title == "Test"; assert len(s.Enum) == 2; assert s.HasConst == true; assert s.Nullable == true

criteria.condition: schema.Parse encounters JSON keywords not directly modeled by Schema fields
criteria.action: preserve the unmodeled keywords in Schema.Extra while retaining their declaration order
criteria.contract: Schema.Extra contains all unmodeled keywords with values matching source JSON; the declaration order of unmodeled keywords in Schema.Extra is preserved

setup: a JSON Schema string containing unmodeled keywords '$comment', 'x-custom', 'deprecated' in order
check.pseudocode: raw := []byte(`{"type":"object","$comment":"note","x-custom":"val","deprecated":true}`); s, err := schema.Parse(raw); assert err == nil; assert s.Extra["$comment"] == "note"; assert s.Extra["x-custom"] == "val"; assert s.Extra["deprecated"] == true

criteria.condition: schema.Parse is invoked with syntactically malformed JSON bytes or unclosed tokens
criteria.action: reject parsing and return an error detailing the syntax failure
criteria.contract: returns nil *Schema and non-nil error

setup: a malformed JSON Schema byte slice with an unclosed object token
check.pseudocode: raw := []byte(`{"type":"object","properties":{`); s, err := schema.Parse(raw); assert s == nil; assert err != nil

requirements.title: Schema Constraint Validation and Coercion
requirements.rationale: Complete JSON Schema constraint validation and type coercion close issue 87 gaps for direct and code mode script execution.

criteria.condition: Validate is called on an object containing properties not listed in Properties or PropertyOrder when AdditionalProperties has Allowed set to false
criteria.action: reject the object and report an unpermitted property error
criteria.contract: returns non-nil error mentioning property not allowed

setup: a Schema configured with AdditionalProperties Allowed set to false and declared property 'name'
check.pseudocode: s := schema.Object(schema.Prop("name", schema.String())).Closed(); err := schema.Validate(s, map[string]any{"name": "test", "extra": 123}); assert err != nil; assert strings.Contains(err.Error(), "not allowed")

criteria.condition: Validate is called on a value that does not match any declared Enum literal in value and type
criteria.action: reject the value and report an enum mismatch error
criteria.contract: returns non-nil error indicating value must be one of declared enum choices

setup: a Schema with Enum values ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT']
check.pseudocode: s := schema.Object(schema.Prop("method", schema.Enum("m", "GET", "POST", "PUT"))); err := schema.Validate(s, map[string]any{"method": "get"}); assert err != nil; assert strings.Contains(err.Error(), "one of")

criteria.condition: Validate is called on a numeric value violating declared Minimum, Maximum, ExclusiveMinimum, ExclusiveMaximum, or MultipleOf constraints
criteria.action: reject the numeric value and report a bound violation error
criteria.contract: returns non-nil error indicating relational constraint violation

setup: a Schema specifying Minimum 10, Maximum 50, and MultipleOf 5
check.pseudocode: s := schema.Object(schema.Prop("num", schema.Int().Min(10).Max(50))); errLow := schema.Validate(s, map[string]any{"num": 5}); assert errLow != nil; assert strings.Contains(errLow.Error(), "at least"); errHigh := schema.Validate(s, map[string]any{"num": 60}); assert errHigh != nil; assert strings.Contains(errHigh.Error(), "at most")

criteria.condition: Validate is called on a string violating MinLength, MaxLength, or failing to match Pattern
criteria.action: reject the string and report a string constraint error
criteria.contract: returns non-nil error indicating length or regex pattern mismatch

setup: a Schema specifying MinLength 5, MaxLength 10, and Pattern '^[a-z]+$'
check.pseudocode: s := &schema.Schema{Type: schema.TypeString, MinLength: ptr(5), MaxLength: ptr(10), Pattern: "^[a-z]+$"}; errShort := schema.Validate(s, "abc"); assert errShort != nil; errPattern := schema.Validate(s, "abc123"); assert errPattern != nil

criteria.condition: Validate is called on an array violating MinItems, MaxItems, or containing duplicate items when UniqueItems is true
criteria.action: reject the array and report an array constraint error
criteria.contract: returns non-nil error indicating cardinality or uniqueness violation

setup: a Schema specifying MinItems 2, MaxItems 4, and UniqueItems true
check.pseudocode: s := schema.Array(schema.Int()); s.MinItems = ptr(2); s.MaxItems = ptr(4); s.UniqueItems = ptr(true); errDup := schema.Validate(s, []any{1, 1}); assert errDup != nil; errShort := schema.Validate(s, []any{1}); assert errShort != nil

criteria.condition: Coerce parses string representations of valid numbers or booleans matching the target schema
criteria.action: convert the strings into numeric or boolean representations and record Coercion entries
criteria.contract: the converted map contains numeric 42.5 and boolean true; the returned coercions list contains entries for each converted field

setup: a Schema with integer, number, and boolean properties
check.pseudocode: s := schema.Object(schema.Prop("n", schema.Number()), schema.Prop("b", schema.Boolean())); out, coercions := schema.Coerce(s, map[string]any{"n": "42.5", "b": "true"}); assert out["n"] == 42.5; assert out["b"] == true; assert len(coercions) == 2

criteria.condition: Coerce encounters non-standard string representations such as NaN, Inf, +5, .5, 5., or 1_0 targeting a number or integer schema
criteria.action: refuse numeric coercion so invalid literals are not emitted into arguments
criteria.contract: returns unchanged value without emitting non-standard numeric literals

setup: a Schema expecting an integer property 'count'
check.pseudocode: s := schema.Object(schema.Prop("count", schema.Int())); for _, bad := range []string{"NaN", "Inf", "+5", ".5", "5.", "1_0"} { out, coercions := schema.Coerce(s, map[string]any{"count": bad}); assert out["count"] == bad; assert len(coercions) == 0 }

requirements.title: Pure-Function Shell Guard and Hook Adapter
requirements.rationale: Decoupling program authorization into a pure function enables host verification while providing a clean execution hook adapter.

criteria.action: define Decision struct containing Block of type bool, Reason of type string, and Terminate of type bool
criteria.contract: guard.Decision contains Block bool, Reason string, and Terminate bool; guard.ShellToolNames equals []string{"execute", "run_command"}

setup: guard package declarations in guard/guard.go
check.pseudocode: d := guard.Decision{Block: true, Reason: "test", Terminate: true}; assert typeof(d.Block) == bool; assert typeof(d.Reason) == string; assert typeof(d.Terminate) == bool; assert guard.ShellToolNames == []string{"execute", "run_command"}

criteria.condition: Check is called with an empty argv slice
criteria.action: return a Decision blocking execution with Reason set to empty argv and Terminate set to opts.TerminateOnBlock
criteria.contract: returns Decision{Block: true, Reason: "empty argv", Terminate: opts.TerminateOnBlock}

setup: guard.Options with TerminateOnBlock set to true
check.pseudocode: opts := guard.Options{TerminateOnBlock: true}; d := guard.Check([]string{}, opts); assert d == guard.Decision{Block: true, Reason: "empty argv", Terminate: true}

criteria.condition: Check evaluates argv[0] containing a path separator that does not match an exact cleaned path in opts.AllowedPrograms
criteria.action: return a Decision blocking execution with Reason reporting that the program is not on the allowlist
criteria.contract: returns Decision{Block: true, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("program %q is not on the allowlist", argv[0]), Terminate: opts.TerminateOnBlock}

setup: guard.Options with AllowedPrograms ['/usr/bin/git'] and TerminateOnBlock true
check.pseudocode: opts := guard.Options{AllowedPrograms: []string{"/usr/bin/git"}, TerminateOnBlock: true}; d := guard.Check([]string{"/usr/bin/curl", "url"}, opts); assert d == guard.Decision{Block: true, Reason: fmt.Sprintf(`program %q is not on the allowlist`, "/usr/bin/curl"), Terminate: true}

criteria.condition: Check evaluates a bare program name argv[0] that does not match any bare program in opts.AllowedPrograms
criteria.action: return a Decision blocking execution with Reason reporting that the bare program is not on the allowlist
criteria.contract: returns Decision{Block: true, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("program %q is not on the allowlist", argv[0]), Terminate: opts.TerminateOnBlock}

setup: guard.Options with AllowedPrograms ['git', 'go'] and TerminateOnBlock false
check.pseudocode: opts := guard.Options{AllowedPrograms: []string{"git", "go"}, TerminateOnBlock: false}; d := guard.Check([]string{"rm", "-rf", "dir"}, opts); assert d == guard.Decision{Block: true, Reason: fmt.Sprintf(`program %q is not on the allowlist`, "rm"), Terminate: false}

criteria.condition: Check evaluates argv[0] that matches an authorized entry in opts.AllowedPrograms
criteria.action: return a Decision permitting execution with Block set to false
criteria.contract: Check returns Decision with Block false

setup: guard.Options with AllowedPrograms ['git', '/usr/local/bin/deploy']
check.pseudocode: opts := guard.Options{AllowedPrograms: []string{"git", "/usr/local/bin/deploy"}}; dBare := guard.Check([]string{"git", "status"}, opts); assert dBare.Block == false; dPath := guard.Check([]string{"/usr/local/bin/deploy"}, opts); assert dPath.Block == false

criteria.action: set ShellToolNames to []string{"execute", "run_command"}

criteria.condition: Restricted creates a BeforeToolCall hook and receives a tool invocation
criteria.action: evaluate blocked tools, shell operators, and environment prefix assignments before delegating program evaluation to Check
criteria.contract: call to secret_tool is blocked with refusal reason; call to execute with pipe operator is blocked; call to execute with dangerous env assignment prefix is blocked; call to execute with allowed program succeeds without block

setup: guard.Options with BlockedTools ['danger_tool'], AllowShellOperators false, AllowEnvPrefixes false, and AllowedPrograms ['git']
check.pseudocode: opts := guard.Options{BlockedTools: []string{"danger_tool"}, AllowShellOperators: false, AllowEnvPrefixes: false, AllowedPrograms: []string{"git"}}; hook := guard.Restricted(opts); decBlocked := hook(ctx, core.BeforeToolCallContext{ToolName: "danger_tool"}); assert decBlocked.Block == true; decPipe := hook(ctx, core.BeforeToolCallContext{ToolName: "execute", Arguments: map[string]any{"command": "git status | cat"}}); assert decPipe.Block == true; decEnv := hook(ctx, core.BeforeToolCallContext{ToolName: "execute", Arguments: map[string]any{"command": "PATH=/tmp git status"}}); assert decEnv.Block == true; decOk := hook(ctx, core.BeforeToolCallContext{ToolName: "execute", Arguments: map[string]any{"command": "git commit"}}); assert decOk.Block == false

requirements.title: Simplified Prompt Assembly
requirements.rationale: Simplifying prompt assembly removes deleted skills dependencies and ensures first-seen tool guideline deduplication.

criteria.action: define Build with signature func Build(system string, tools []core.Tool) string
criteria.contract: Build has signature func Build(system string, tools []core.Tool) string; prompt.Input and prompt.SkillBlocks are not declared; prompt package does not import the skills package

setup: prompt package declarations and imports in prompt/prompt.go
check.pseudocode: var buildFn func(system string, tools []core.Tool) string = prompt.Build; assert buildFn != nil; assert !existsSymbol("prompt.Input"); assert !existsSymbol("prompt.SkillBlocks"); for imp in packageImports("prompt"): assert !strings.Contains(imp, "/skills")

criteria.condition: Build is called with an empty system prompt string
criteria.action: initialize prompt text with BaseInstructions and append UniversalGuidelines
criteria.contract: with empty system prompt, prompt starts with BaseInstructions and UniversalGuidelines; with custom system prompt, custom text replaces BaseInstructions and UniversalGuidelines

setup: empty system prompt string and custom system prompt string
check.pseudocode: pDefault := prompt.Build("", nil); assert strings.HasPrefix(pDefault, prompt.BaseInstructions); assert strings.Contains(pDefault, prompt.UniversalGuidelines[0]); pCustom := prompt.Build("Custom system prompt instructions.", nil); assert strings.HasPrefix(pCustom, "Custom system prompt instructions."); assert !strings.Contains(pCustom, prompt.BaseInstructions)

criteria.condition: Build is called with a non-empty system prompt string
criteria.action: use system prompt as the opening instructions in place of BaseInstructions and UniversalGuidelines

criteria.condition: Build processes tools containing PromptGuidelines
criteria.action: append per-tool guidelines in first-seen order, deduplicating identical guidelines
criteria.contract: per-tool PromptGuidelines are deduplicated and appended in first-seen order; ExecuteFallbackGuideline is appended when execute is present without search tools; SearchOverExecuteGuideline is appended when both execute and search tools are present

setup: tools with duplicate PromptGuidelines and varying combinations of execute and search tools
check.pseudocode: t1 := core.Tool{Name: "t1", PromptGuidelines: []string{"Guideline A", "Guideline B"}}; t2 := core.Tool{Name: "t2", PromptGuidelines: []string{"Guideline B", "Guideline C"}}; res := prompt.Build("", []core.Tool{t1, t2}); idxA := strings.Index(res, "Guideline A"); idxB := strings.Index(res, "Guideline B"); idxC := strings.Index(res, "Guideline C"); assert idxA < idxB && idxB < idxC; assert strings.Count(res, "Guideline B") == 1

criteria.condition: Build processes tools including execute or search tools
criteria.action: append ExecuteFallbackGuideline when execute is present without search tools, or append SearchOverExecuteGuideline when both execute and search tools are present
remove prompt.Input, prompt.SkillBlocks, and all imports of the skills package

execution_paths.title: Order-preserving schema parsing and argument validation pipeline

steps.action: submits an authored JSON Schema byte slice to schema.Parse
parses the schema using jsontext, preserves property declaration order in PropertyOrder, and returns a *Schema
supplies tool call argument bytes to core.PrepareArguments for execution
validates arguments against schema constraints and preserves original input bytes in PreparedArguments.Raw

setup: an authored JSON schema with ordered properties and valid JSON input bytes
end_state: PrepareArguments validates arguments against schema constraints successfully
PreparedArguments.Raw preserves the original tool input bytes verbatim
smoke.pseudocode: schemaBytes := []byte(`{"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string"},"filter":{"type":"string"},"limit":{"type":"integer"}}}`); s, err := schema.Parse(schemaBytes); assert err == nil; assert s.PropertyOrder == []string{"query", "filter", "limit"}; tool := core.Tool{Name: "search", InputSchema: s}; block := core.ToolUseBlock{ID: "t1", Name: "search", Input: json.RawMessage(`{"query":"test","filter":"active","limit":5}`)}; prep, err := core.PrepareArguments(tool, block); assert err == nil; assert bytes.Equal(prep.Raw, block.Input); assert prep.Args["query"] == "test"

execution_paths.title: Pure guard authorization and Restricted tool hook enforcement

steps.action: dispatches a command execution request for run_command through the guard.Restricted hook
extracts argv arguments from the invocation map and delegates evaluation to guard.Check
evaluates argv[0] against opts.AllowedPrograms without side effects and returns a Decision
converts the Decision into a BeforeToolCallDecision reflecting authorization or refusal reason

setup: guard.Options configured with AllowedPrograms ['ls', 'git'] and Restricted hook installed
end_state: Restricted extracts argv and delegates evaluation to guard.Check
guard.Check returns Decision with Block false
Restricted returns BeforeToolCallDecision with Block false permitting execution
smoke.pseudocode: opts := guard.Options{AllowedPrograms: []string{"ls", "git"}}; hook := guard.Restricted(opts); dec := hook(context.Background(), core.BeforeToolCallContext{ToolName: "run_command", Arguments: map[string]any{"argv": []any{"ls", "-la"}}}); assert dec.Block == false

execution_paths.title: Simplified prompt construction and model stream dispatch

steps.action: invokes prompt.Build with configured tools and optional custom system instructions
assembles opening instructions and appends deduplicated tool guidelines in first-seen order
constructs a core.Request with assembled system blocks and dispatches it via core.ProviderClient.Stream
streams StreamEvent values carrying incremental progress and terminal status

setup: tools list with file navigation and execute tools, and a ProviderClient implementation
end_state: assembled prompt contains base instructions and deduplicated guidelines in first-seen order
ProviderClient.Stream accepts Request and returns a channel streaming StreamEvent values to completion
smoke.pseudocode: toolsList := []core.Tool{{Name: "read_file", PromptGuidelines: []string{"Read before editing."}}, {Name: "execute"}}; sysPrompt := prompt.Build("", toolsList); assert strings.Contains(sysPrompt, "Read before editing."); req := core.Request{System: []core.ContentBlock{core.TextBlock{Text: sysPrompt}}}; ch, err := providerClient.Stream(context.Background(), req); assert err == nil; ev := <-ch; assert ev.Err == nil
